title: Module 5 · Lesson 1 — Reasoning strategies and what each one costs

lines: Module Five, Lesson One: reasoning strategies.
Six techniques, each with a price tag and a phrase that gives it away.
Picture an HR help bot at a company of two thousand people.
To make it smarter, the team sends every question through Tree of Thoughts.
Now a question about vacation days takes thirty seconds.
The bill grows tenfold, and the answers are no better.
Chain of thought is the cheapest: one linear reasoning path before the answer.
It costs one to two times the baseline, and the phrase is: think step by step.
Self-consistency samples several chains and takes a majority vote.
Sample five chains, and you pay five times.
Tree of Thoughts branches, scores partial solutions, searches, and backtracks.
At five to twenty times the baseline, it is the priciest of the six.
It fits only when exploring branches helps, and the model can score partial states.
Without that score there is nothing to search on, so never use it for a quick lookup.
Chain of Verification drafts an answer, asks itself checking questions, then revises.
It costs three to four times, and it targets factual errors.
Reflexion writes a self-critique after a failure and keeps it for the next attempt.
Debate has agents argue positions while a judge decides.
Modern reasoning models already think internally.
Adding a step by step prompt duplicates that work, so a simple lookup needs no scaffold at all.
Treat reasoning effort as a routed decision, not a constant.
Easy requests get a direct answer, medium ones get chain of thought, and only hard ones get voting or search.
A confidence estimate or a small classifier picks the lane.
It is the same routing idea used to choose models.
And the HR bot still gets the new parental leave policy wrong.
Reasoning cannot invent a fact the model never had, so the fix is retrieval.
On the exam, match the phrase to the technique, and distrust expensive reasoning offered for a knowledge gap.
The full cost table is waiting in the lesson below.
